Properly quote schema and table names (#93, @CyberDem0n)

    Replace manual double-quote and single-quote string concatenation with
    quote_identifier()/quote_ident() and quote_literal_cstr() when building
    dynamic SQL for ANALYZE statements and log/error inserts.

    Since `squeeze.worker_role` is supposed to be a superuser, lack of
    proper quoting allows executing arbitrary SQL with superuser privileges.

## Highlights

v0.19.2 is v0.19.1 plus one fix: **a reference that names the wrong collection never opens a different item** (BUG-4119). A ref such as `TASK-42` used to fall back to "item number 42 in any collection" when no collection with that prefix had it, so a stale or mistyped ref, or a wiki link such as `[[TASK-42]]`, could resolve to an unrelated item and write a wrong link. A ref now resolves only through its own prefix, or through the move history of an item that left that collection.

**Behaviour

**CLI and MCP correctness.** `pad item list --format json` pages to completion when `--limit` isn't set (BUG-4024). MCP numeric parameters are checked strictly on both transports: a non-number or non-integer is refused instead of being dropped or changed (BUG-4056, BUG-4061, BUG-4065, BUG-4070). `pad session list` reads "unknown" instead of "dead" across a PID namespace (BUG-4090). A relative `PAD_DATA_DIR` or `PAD_DB_PATH` now warns (BUG-4066).

Postgres.js 4 is out, and this release lets you install it alongside the dialect without peer dependency warnings. The `postgres` peer range is now `>= 3.4.0 < 5`, and the test suite runs against both 3.x and 4.x on every Node.js and Bun version we support.
* feat: support postgres v4. by @igalklebanov in https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely-postgres-js/commit/19ee1ea
Nothing changed in the dialect itself; everything it relies on behaves the same on 4. Postgres.js 4 does change a few things for your own que

This patch brings the dialect in line with Kysely 0.29.8's transaction fixes for PostgreSQL.
Commits that PostgreSQL answers with `ROLLBACK`, because an earlier statement error left the transaction aborted, now reject with Kysely's `AbortedTransactionError` instead of resolving as if committed. This requires `kysely` >= 0.29.8; on older versions the behavior is unchanged.
* fix: reject commits that roll back aborted transactions. by @igalklebanov in https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely-postgres-js/pull/470

Parameterless raw and schema queries now use postgres.js's `unsafe()` defaults. Query-builder `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `MERGE` queries, plus any query with parameters, retain prepared execution. Instance-level `postgres({ prepare: false })` remains respected.
* fix: preserve parameterless raw query batches by @igalklebanov in https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely-postgres-js/pull/466 (fixes https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely-postgres-js/issues/465)
* chore: bump dependencies. by @igalkle

This release fixes a misalignment of expectations in the dialect's driver with how people normally use `postgres` and it's defaults which caused all queries to not use prepared statements and always re-plan.
Now, this dialect prepares everything under the hood, but still respects `prepare: false` in `postgres` instance. This should somewhat speed up your recurring queries.
* feat: enable prepared statements for query execution. by @igalklebanov in https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely-postgres-js/pull/464

- Fixed automations.yaml being corrupted after a bulk action. Rewrites of the retention automation could overlap and share one temporary file. They now go through one at a time, wait for a bulk action to settle, use a private temp file, check the result parses first, and keep a copy of the previous file as `automations.yaml.dbs_backup`.
